seoTitle: How to Turn Off Automatic Relisting on eBay in 2026
metaDescription: Tired of unsold eBay items relisting themselves? Here's how to switch off automatic relisting for single or bulk listings, with real settings shown.
intro: Automatic relisting can quietly rack up fees and clutter your eBay store when unsold items keep reposting without your say-so. This guide shows how to reach the relisting controls through My eBay and the Seller Hub, and how to update the setting across many listings at once instead of opening each one individually. It also covers the difference between Good 'Til Cancelled and Manual listings, since that distinction changes how the relist setting actually behaves on a given item.

steps.heading: Get to your Selling area through My eBay
steps.body: From the My eBay Activity page — reachable from the account menu at the top of any eBay page — the left sidebar lists Summary, Recently viewed, Bids & offers, Watchlist, Purchases, Saved feed, Saved searches, Saved sellers, and further down, Selling. Selling is the entry point for everything covered in this guide, since relisting behavior is a per-listing seller setting, not a buyer-facing one.

image.caption: The My eBay Activity page sidebar, with Selling listed among Bids & offers, Watchlist, and Purchases — the path into your listings and their settings.

steps.heading: Open Seller Hub and find Selling preferences
steps.body: Selling opens into Seller Hub, where a second sidebar on the listings page groups Drafts, Scheduled, and Ended above a SETTINGS section containing Selling preferences, Listing templates, and Business policies. Selling preferences is where account-wide defaults live, including how unsold listings behave by default — this is the setting to change first if you want new listings to stop relisting automatically going forward.

image.caption: The Seller Hub listings table, with Selling preferences visible in the SETTINGS section of the left sidebar, and checkboxes for selecting listings in bulk.

steps.heading: Turn off Automatically Relist in Selling preferences
steps.body: Inside Selling preferences, locate the section covering unsold items and switch "Automatically Relist" off. This changes the default eBay applies to items that end without selling, but it's worth knowing this default mainly governs new listings and renewal behavior — it doesn't necessarily reach back and change every listing you already have live, which is why the next step matters.

steps.heading: Edit active listings individually or select several at once
steps.body: Back on the main Seller Hub listings table, each row has its own checkbox on the left, and the header row includes a select-all checkbox alongside a listing count and totals summary (something like "Results: 1-17 of 17" with total value and quantity). Check the box on a single listing to edit its relist setting alone, or check the header box to select everything in view, then use the Edit or Actions button above the table to apply the change across all selected listings in one pass instead of opening each one.

steps.heading: Know the difference between Good 'Til Cancelled and Manual listings
steps.body: Good 'Til Cancelled listings are eBay's default for fixed-price items and renew on a recurring basis — typically monthly — until they sell or you cancel them, which is a form of relisting that runs somewhat independently of the Automatically Relist toggle since it's built into how the listing type itself works. Manual listings, more common for auction-style items, only relist when you explicitly choose to relist them, so if you're seeing unwanted reposts specifically, check whether the listing in question is Good 'Til Cancelled first.

steps.heading: Set your default so future listings don't relist automatically
steps.body: With Selling preferences updated and your current listings edited, new items you create going forward should follow the new default instead of reverting to automatic relisting. It's worth spot-checking a newly created listing's settings after this change once, just to confirm the preference actually carried through, since eBay's defaults can vary slightly by listing format and category.

faq.question: Will turning off automatic relisting affect my current active listings?
faq.answer: Not automatically. Changing the default in Selling preferences mainly governs new listings and future renewals, so you'll typically need to select your current active listings in Seller Hub — individually or in bulk using the checkboxes — and update the relist setting on them directly.

faq.question: What's the difference between Good 'Til Cancelled and Manual listings on eBay?
faq.answer: Good 'Til Cancelled listings renew automatically on a recurring basis until they sell or you cancel them, since renewal is built into that listing format. Manual listings only relist when you choose to relist them yourself, which gives you more direct control over reposting.

faq.question: Does automatic relisting cost extra in fees?
faq.answer: Relisting can trigger new listing fees each time an item reposts, which is one of the main reasons sellers turn the feature off, especially for items that have been sitting unsold across several relist cycles.

faq.question: Can I turn off relisting for multiple items at once?
faq.answer: Yes. In Seller Hub's listings table, check the box next to each listing you want to change, or use the header checkbox to select everything visible, then use the Edit or Actions button above the table to apply the change in bulk.

faq.question: Where exactly do I find the relisting setting on eBay?
faq.answer: Go to My eBay > Selling to open Seller Hub, then look for Selling preferences in the SETTINGS section of the left sidebar — that's where the account-wide Automatically Relist default lives, separate from any per-listing edits you make in the main table.
